items.title: Sid Davilla Interview, 1969-04-17
items.q: I was the first guy to put, sounds like this and there for me, first guy to put Sweet Emma back on the street.

ctx.x: I can see just from seeing that, it's difficult for them, for anybody to make it to that kind of music, because I know they didn't really have any big business down there.

No, it's a difficult thing, I mean, what you'd like to have and what you can afford, I guess, to see, uh, whether it's, uh, trying to run a nightclub with entertainment or, uh, buying an automobile, I guess you've got to do what you can afford to do. Of course, we tried, we tried, and we, uh, we were so happy with it. It was a wonderful sight to walk in this place and see some, uh, genuinely happy people looking up and seeing some faces on the stage, like, uh, George Lewis, Papa Selesdan, Joe Robichaud, uh, oh,…
She became quite a hit, right? Mm-hmm. Yeah. Well, I think that's about it with just about attitude.
